clue.text: Abrasive rocks cropped wild cat earlier

indicators.note: says the cat comes before the frozen rocks in the answer, though it follows them in the clue
a cropped thing has had its tail cut short, so the big cat's name loses its final letter

parts.note: the puma is an American wild cat
ice cubes in a drink are 'rocks', as in whisky on the rocks

explanation.surface: Someone describes rough stones and a wild animal seen beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumice is a light volcanic stone used for scouring and smoothing, so it serves as an abrasive.

clue.text: Delay travelling north, up to French city

indicators.note: in a down entry, travelling north means the word up is written bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
Nice is a city on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: A journey northwards is postponed until reaching a city in France.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'travelling north' means reading upwards, so only the short word 'up' is turned; 'to' stays as written.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something on ice is an idiom for postponing it or holding it in reserve.

clue.text: Amount of power needed to cook game was endless — temperature doubled

indicators.note: cooking something works it over, so these letters are reshaped into a new order
the word was loses its last letter
the single temperature letter appears twice in a row

explanation.surface: A recipe says how much energy a game dish needs, with the oven heat doubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cook' rearranges GAME plus WA ('was endless') into MEGAWA; 'doubled' gives TT.
explanation.definitionFit: A megawatt is a unit of a million watts, a measured quantity of electrical power.

clue.text: Old King's order — salad

parts.note: Old King Cole is the merry old soul of the nursery rhyme, so his possessive gives this name plus S
law and order go together; a law is an order or rule

explanation.surface: A command from an ancient monarch concerns a side dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Old King Cole is a British nursery-rhyme king, a merry old soul who called for his pipe and bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleslaw is a salad of shredded raw cabbage in dressing.

clue.text: Bill attends Kasbah regularly, along with an expert

parts.note: a bill is an advertisement, shortened to ad

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, here the second, fourth and sixth of Kasbah

parts.note: and means along with

explanation.surface: Someone called Bill frequents a North African citadel together with a skilled companion.
explanation.definitionFit: A dab hand is a British idiom for someone highly skilled at something.

clue.text: Called companion about accommodation

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for companion is read backwards

parts.note: bud is informal American for a pal or companion
a bed for the night is accommodation, as in bed and breakfast

explanation.surface: A friend phoned about somewhere to stay.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubbed means named or given a nickname, the same as called.

clue.text: Smell blood after duke produces punch

indicators.note: blood relatives are placed after the duke's letter

parts.note: BO is body odour, an unpleasant smell
one's blood is one's kin, family by descent

explanation.surface: A whiff of blood following a nobleman leads to a blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punch' looks like a blow, but here it is the tool that pierces holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodkin is a blunt needle or small pointed tool for punching holes in cloth or leather.

clue.text: Plant extremists attached to a meadow

parts.note: the extremes of the alphabet run from A to Z
taken as written
lea is a poetic word for a meadow or grassy field

explanation.surface: Radicals are fixed to a piece of grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: The azalea is a flowering shrub related to the rhododendron, so a plant.

clue.text: Wed perhaps outside — one books small cake?

indicators.note: the day word sits outside, around the other letters

parts.note: Wed is short for Wednesday, an example of a day
I is the Roman numeral one
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A wedding outdoors, with someone ordering petite cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wed' reads as a verb for getting married; it is the abbreviated weekday.
explanation.definitionFit: A dainty is a delicacy, especially a small fancy cake or sweetmeat.

clue.text: Switch to goods connected with the French

parts.note: taken as written
G stands for good, so goods in the plural doubles it
le is the French masculine form of the

explanation.surface: Changing to merchandise that is linked with France.
explanation.definitionFit: A toggle is a switch that flips between two states, as in a toggle switch.

clue.text: A friend snubbed custom here in Middle East

parts.note: taken as written
bud is informal for a friend

indicators.note: a snub nose is short, so the word for custom is cut short at its end

parts.note: a habit is a custom or practice

explanation.definitionFit: Abu Dhabi is the capital of the United Arab Emirates, a place in the Middle East.

clue.text: Quite modern Tyneside institute mum joins

parts.note: Tyneside is in North East England, abbreviated NE
the WI is the Women's Institute, a British community organisation
mum means silent, and sh is a call for silence

explanation.surface: A northern institute that a mother joins is fairly up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like a mother but means keeping quiet. The Women's Institute is a British organisation for women, known for jam and community work.
explanation.definitionFit: Newish means fairly new, so somewhat modern rather than fully so.

clue.text: Grey borders in extension covered by dearest architectural feature

indicators.note: the pet word covers, enclosing the inner letters

parts.note: a pet is a dearest or favourite person
grey and dim both mean dull or poorly lit

explanation.surface: Grey edging on an extension, paid for by the most expensive builder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dearest' reads as most costly but means a darling, PET.
explanation.definitionFit: A pediment is the triangular gable above a classical portico, a feature of buildings.

clue.text: Churchman, out of love, meets Greek character turning over veg

parts.note: a parson is a clergyman, a churchman
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

clue.text: Fine characters half involved in road rage

parts.note: F is short for fine, as on pencil grades

indicators.note: takes the second half of the letters of the word road

explanation.surface: A fine for drivers involved in a fit of temper on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'road rage' looks like one phrase but 'rage' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rage is a craze, the latest thing everyone wants, as in all the rage.

clue.text: Worker retires into Crown for rest

indicators.note: the reversed worker goes into the crown word

parts.note: a cap is a crown, as a dental crown or the top of something

indicators.note: retires means draws back, so the insect word is reversed

parts.note: the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A labourer goes back to the palace for a break.
explanation.definitionFit: A catnap is a short sleep, a brief rest.

clue.text: School party pedal back

indicators.note: both pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: a do is a party
P is the abbreviation for pedal in piano music

explanation.surface: A school outing where someone cycles home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' looks like a place of learning, but it means a group of whales.
explanation.definitionFit: A pod is a group of whales or dolphins, like a school of fish.

clue.text: Rush ballet leap, stubbing toe

indicators.note: the toe is the foot, the last letter, which is cut off

parts.note: a jete is a jump from one foot to the other in ballet

explanation.surface: A dancer hurts their foot during a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: To jet is to rush or travel fast, as a jet of water spurts.

clue.text: Get married, restricting gold frills to shirt material

or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: the frills of something are its edges, so the outer letters of shirt

explanation.definitionFit: Worsted is a smooth woollen yarn and the cloth woven from it, a material.

clue.text: Shout of annoyance interrupts another, before end of this game

indicators.note: breaking into the middle of the other exclamation

parts.note: drat is another exclamation of annoyance
ugh is a cry of disgust or annoyance

indicators.note: the last letter of the word this

explanation.surface: Someone shouting in irritation keeps breaking off before this game ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another shout of annoyance, DRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Draughts is the British board game called checkers in America.

clue.text: Seaman, then another, reported one clinging to cliff-face?

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the letters come from how the words are said

parts.note: an able seaman is an AB, and another seaman is a sailor, said together as one word

explanation.surface: Two seafarers are said to have clung to a sheer rock face.
explanation.definitionFit: An abseiler descends a cliff by rope, so is someone hanging on a rock face.

clue.text: City embraced by traveller joining unknown rally

indicators.note: the city letters are held inside the traveller word

parts.note: a rover is a wanderer or traveller

Y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.walkthrough: 'rally' looks like a car race but it means a revival.
explanation.definitionFit: A rally is a recovery, as when prices or a patient pick up again.

clue.text: Shake, when squandering a thousand for this bet?

indicators.note: squandering means losing, so the thousand letter is dropped

parts.note: to tremble is to shake
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A gambler shakes after losing a grand on this wager.
explanation.definitionFit: A treble is a bet on three races, all of which must win.

clue.text: State entered between Arizona and Hawaii

definitions.text: State entered between Arizona and Hawaii

parts.words: State entered between Arizona and Hawaii
parts.note: Arizona joined the US as the 48th state and Hawaii as the 50th, so the one admitted between them was 49th

explanation.definitionFit: Alaska was admitted to the US in 1959, after Arizona in 1912 and just before Hawaii.

clue.text: Legal section periodically call at practice

indicators.note: periodically means taking letters at intervals, here alternate letters of call at

parts.note: use and practice both mean customary habit

explanation.surface: A section of law about phoning during training sessions.
explanation.definitionFit: A clause is a section of a legal document such as a contract or statute.

clue.text: Aircraft noise envelops old commandos ascending

indicators.note: in a down entry, ascending means the whole is written upwards
the noise word wraps round the other letters

parts.note: din is a loud noise
RM is the Royal Marines, the British commando force

explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'ascending' reads the whole built word upwards, so the noise-around-troops word DORMIN appears backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nimrod was a British RAF maritime patrol aircraft.

clue.text: Peg leg

definitions.meaning: a peg is a small fastener, such as a clothes or tent fastener

clue.text: Try and see cartoon character

to eye is to look at or see

explanation.surface: A suggestion to have a go and watch an animated figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Popeye the Sailor Man is a spinach-eating cartoon character.

clue.text: Confectionery supply, including lozenge, handed back

the supply word includes the lozenge word inside it

clue.text: Pronounced pleats — the latest in fashionable party jacket

clue.text: Landowner grabbing right and left — typical hoarder

parts.note: a squire is a country landowner

clue.text: He's munching nothing except duck, that's put aside

clue.text: Huge nose entertains English bird
